% ITEM 1 — Implementation cross-check (V3).
% TARGET: \subsection{Verification}  (label sec:fem_verification).
%   (a) change the opening "...by four independent checks" -> "five independent checks".
%   (b) insert the sentence below as check (v), immediately BEFORE the existing
%       "Finally, the growth column used for the production results below is
%        mesh-converged ...".
%   (c) add the table row below to Table~\ref{tab:fem_verification}.
% ---------------------------------------------------------------------

(v)~The production growth--stress field is reproduced by a \emph{second, independently
coded} constitutive routine: an alternative UMAT built on a neo-Hookean rather than a
Hencky elastic potential, but sharing the same isotropic growth split
$\bF_{\!g}=(1+\alpha)\bI$, returns the constrained growth-induced stress of the confined
collar to within $0.1\%$ of the production implementation, confirming that the reported
stresses carry no implementation-specific artefact.

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------
% ITEM 2 — Upgrade the constitutive-extension outlook from "future work" to
% "implemented and verified" for the viscoelastic case.
% TARGET: \subsection{Relation to prior art, validation, and limits}
%   (label sec:fem_validation), the "Outlook" paragraph.
% ACTION: replace the existing sentence
%   "And the crude neo-Hookean elastic factor can be replaced by the worm-like-chain
%    network model of EPS mechanics~\cite{EhretBol2013} for a more physical constitutive
%    law that captures the strain-stiffening the present model omits."
% with the sentence below.
% ---------------------------------------------------------------------

The crude neo-Hookean elastic factor can be refined towards a more physical constitutive
law along two axes. For the equilibrium response, the worm-like-chain network model of EPS
mechanics~\cite{EhretBol2013} captures the strain-stiffening the present model omits. For
the rate-dependent response, a finite-strain viscoelastic extension
$\bF=\bF_{\!e}\bF_{\!v}\bF_{\!g}$ has already been implemented and verified
(\texttt{umat\_biofilm\_visco.f}): its exact algorithmic tangent, obtained by
deformation-gradient perturbation~\cite{SunChaikof2008}, reproduces a central-difference
reference to a relative error of $2.4$--$2.9\times10^{-8}$ across the elastic,
viscoelastic, and Mooney--Rivlin test cases and preserves the quadratic convergence of the
global Newton solve, so the viscoelastic law is a drop-in replacement rather than an open
modelling question.
